method: Built-in image generation; model identifier unavailable. No paid API execution.

prompts.center: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: transparent side-scroller environment plate, wide 3:1 canvas 2160x720. Input 1 is the preferred substantial maze (edit target); input 2 the photographic material reference. Preserve the maze's broad pale blue-green riveted girder platforms, tall stone shafts, connected horizontal bridges, meaningful empty chambers, ladders and side branches. NOT thin pipes beneath a giant bridge. Refine this CENTER maze into a readable journey: broad bottom entry on left at y=530; two tall climbable ladder shafts; open central reconnection court with an elevated optional dead-end balcony; long upper bridge; generous headroom above all walks, connected lower return path; broad right exit at y=530. Side elevation, no vanishing point. Keep substantial concrete buttresses rooted at y=610; water and creek will be composited separately, so do NOT draw any water, reflections, sky, far trees or ground beneath this structure. Keep outermost 160 pixels on BOTH sides a simple level broad girder walkway at top y=530 with footings beneath to y=610, no ladders or tall projections in those edge zones, so modules connect. Every ladder must meet a platform at both ends. Architecture mostly occupies y=120..610, leaving sky headroom. Pixel art, crisp rounded vegetation and readable materials matching reference. Remove ALL plants, vines, moss clumps and railings from the foreground plate; subtle moss stains in stone are fine. No gates, characters, text, labels, checkerboard, glow or FX. Transparent empty spaces and background. Render an art plate, not a diagram.

prompts.plants: Use case: background-extraction. Asset type: transparent wide 3:1 pixel-art foliage plate 2160x720. References are the rusted creek maze and photographic material collage. Draw ONLY separate green/golden ivy and leafy clumps that can be placed over stone buttresses and creek bank. Keep the top 420 pixels empty. Place low mounds and hanging clumps in the bottom y=460..620 with large transparent gaps between them. NO structures, stone, metal, columns, ladders, dark rectangles, ground, water, red outlines, solid shadows or backdrop. Opaque colorful leaf interiors with genuinely clean transparent perimeter. This is a foreground layer, so each clump must have a crisp independent silhouette. Not a sheet of unrelated props: compose a single continuous loose overgrown riverbank edge. Match the lush warm pixel painting, no text.
prompts.repair-left-center:
Repair one actual join of the scene-first broad steel and masonry; separate after seam repair layer in a flat side-scrolling pixel-art stage. Image 1 is the exact staggered context canvas, not a style reference. The seam lies at x=1080. Change only the band x=[824,1336); image 2 shows the edit mask (transparent means editable). Continue existing silhouettes, steel edges, foliage, waterlines or reflections as appropriate; connect matching platform ends without deleting branches or inventing a new camera. Keep every pixel outside the band, original scale, palette and flat projection. Transparent holes stay transparent; no matte, labels, HUD, glow or new scenery layer. Output the complete 2160x720 context canvas, not a tight crop. Connect the broad low deck at y=460 across this join, preserving footings down to y=630 and matching edge heights at both sides of the editable band. No thin bars, foliage, red matte fringes, water, sky or new towers. Keep opening/headroom and transparent background.

Edit target image1 is the exact join context; supporting image2 is edit mask. Keep canvas 2160x720. Repair only x824..1336: a continuous broad riveted low bridge top, including its rooted stone plinth, connects the two panels. Preserve all other image geometry; transparency in empty areas. Match the TOP SURFACE at both protected edges of that band; a gentle step if needed, not a floating disconnected deck. Remove red/yellow matte-colored fringe in the editable band. No sky, trees, water, new structures or plants.
